# @emergentbase/overlay

Emergent's in-pod overlay: a **dev-server-only** Vite plugin injected into generated app previews. Ships branded error UI today; designed as the general injection point for future in-preview capabilities (session capture, E1ectron-driven tooling).

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { emergentOverlay } from "@emergentbase/overlay/vite";
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [emergentOverlay()],
  server: { hmr: { overlay: false } }, // hand build-error rendering to the overlay
});
```

## What it does

- **Branded error overlay** (classic inline script — survives total module-graph failure): runtime errors (`window error` / `unhandledrejection`, React 19 `reportError` path), build errors (live via `/@vite/client` hot context; Vite 8 keeps no error buffer, so a server-side per-module cache covers fresh page loads), resource load failures. Light/dark follows the app (html.dark class → painted-background luminance at viewport center → light).
- **Sourcemap resolution**: request/reply over Vite's hot channel (`emergent-overlay:resolve` / `:resolved`) rewrites runtime stacks to original source positions (module-graph transform maps) with a code frame.
- **Probe API**: `GET /__emergent_overlay__/health` → `200` clean / `503` with `build_error` + per-page runtime errors (page reports arrive over Vite's token-authenticated hot channel — `emergent-overlay:report` — 15s heartbeat, 45s TTL, seq-ordered; no open HTTP write endpoints). `splash_visible` / `splash_in_source` report whether the stock template splash is still up (informational; keyed off a `data-emergent-splash` DOM marker). Don't pass `curl -f` — it discards the 503 diagnostic body.
- **Parent-frame events**: `postMessage` in the `preview-logger` protocol with `via: "emergent-overlay"` provenance — the E1ectron preview panel's fix-it chip keys on this.
- **Buffer-mode recorder asset** is served as `/__emergent_overlay__/recorder.js` — never `rrweb.js`, which EasyPrivacy (default in uBlock Origin, AdGuard, Brave) blocks by name. If a blocker still drops it, the overlay stays quiet: no error card, bug FAB hidden, crash reports stack-only with a digest that says the recorder was blocked (not "off").
- **Bug button** (`EMERGENT_OVERLAY_FAB=on`, shown only once the recorder is live) is styled as a sibling of the builder's edit toolbar (visual-edit-v2 tokens). Inside the builder it posts `userBugReport` to the host, which prefills the chat — the user presses send ("Added to your chat"). Opened directly nothing reaches the agent, so it saves the report to the workspace and offers "Copy note": a ready-to-paste line with the digest path ("Saved to your workspace"). Hover reveals the toolbar's chevron: it tucks the button below the edge and leaves a small tab that brings it back (session-scoped, like the toolbar's own collapse).
- **Fails open, never blames the app.** Every server hook and route is wrapped: a broken hook serves the page untouched, a broken probe answers 200 `{degraded}`, HMR bookkeeping can never stand between Vite and its client. The client ignores errors from its own capture layer, browser extensions, opaque cross-origin scripts, cross-origin resource load failures, and browser/OS-injected noise (Safari/iOS autofill, a gesture-less clipboard write, Chromium internal-bug strings) (an ad-blocked analytics beacon or a CDN font is not the app's fault; a library that is really missing surfaces as a runtime error), and disables itself after one internal exception. `npm run smoke` (CI on every PR and before every publish) packs the tarball, installs it into a scratch Vite app, boots it and probes `/`, `/health`, the recorder asset and a real browser boot — the dud-tarball class cannot ship.
- **No hot channel, no recorder.** With Vite `hmr: false` (pods started with `ENABLE_RELOAD=false`) nothing could ever flush the buffer, so the Vite adapter skips the recorder tag and the client skips recording: the error card still shows, the bug button stays off, and no recording is written.
- **The overlay never produces a failed request in the browser.** Its own probe fetches use `/__emergent_overlay__/health?client=1` (same JSON, always 200), so an agent's Playwright harness or a user's devtools never lists the overlay next to the app's real error. The platform probe without the flag keeps the 200/503 contract.
- **Session recording (rrweb) injection** — `EMERGENT_OVERLAY_RRWEB=true` additionally injects the recorder loader tags (`/_emergent/rrweb/rrweb.min.js` + `recorder.js`, marker `data-emergent-rrweb`). Asset serving and event ingest live at the preview edge (emergentbase/mono#79 · envcore rrweb branch) — the overlay is only the in-pod injection layer, and it coexists with edge-side injection (both guard on the marker / `__emergentRrwebActive`). Recorder asset failures are excluded from error capture, so enabling this where no edge handler exists degrades silently.
- Escape hatch: `DISABLE_EMERGENT_OVERLAY=true`.

## Dev-only guarantee

The plugin declares `apply: "serve"`: `vite build` output contains **zero** overlay bytes (verified by build+grep). Deployed apps and paused-env static CDN bundles never ship it — same posture as `@emergentbase/visual-edits`.

## Publishing

`Publish` workflow (manual dispatch): bump the version **in your PR**, merge, then dispatch — CI never commits to main (an idempotency guard refuses versions already on the CDN). Publishes to the GitHub npm registry and uploads the tarball to the assets CDN (Cloudflare R2) as `npm/emergentbase-overlay-<version>.tgz` + `-latest.tgz`, so consumers install without registry auth:

```json
"@emergentbase/overlay": "https://assets.emergent.sh/npm/emergentbase-overlay-0.1.0.tgz"
```

## Consumers

- `app-builder` `templates/farm-ts` (emergentbase/app-builder#404)
- E1ectron preview-panel fix-it chip (emergentbase/E1ectron#5059) — reads the postMessage protocol, not the package
